title: Migrants Came Home and Built 1,800 Fortress-Towers — Kaiping | China Travel Expert
description:
They crossed the Pacific, made their fortunes, and came home to build fortresses that look like nothing else in China.

The Kaiping Diaolou are fortified towers in the Wuyi region of Guangdong, raised by overseas Chinese who returned with money and foreign ideas. At their peak there were over 3,000; about 1,800 still stand. Look up and you'll see Roman domes, Greek columns, Baroque railings and medieval battlements sitting above grey village brick and upswept Chinese eaves. They were built for a hard reason — defence against floods and bandits — but they became symbols of a family's success abroad. Locals called the returnees who paid for them "Gold Mountain uncles." UNESCO inscribed five of the villages in 2007.

🧭 Expert Tip: Head to Zili village for the best-preserved cluster — go on a clear morning so the towers reflect in the paddy water, and climb one to see the mix of styles up close.
